simple.meaning: שַׂלְמָה (salmâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a dress.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 22:8. The surrounding context includes righteousness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׂלְמָה (H8008) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שַׂלְמָה (salmâh) / H8008 is traced through Exodus 22:8, Exodus 22:25, Deuteronomy 24:13, Deuteronomy 29:4 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.

timeline.evidenceText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.
“If you lend money to any of my people with you who is poor, you shall not be to him as a creditor. You shall not charge him interest.
You shall surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment and bless you. It shall be righteousness to you before Yahweh your God.
But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
and old and patched sandals on their feet, and wore old garments. All the bread of their food supply was dry and moldy.
These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.”

and spoke to them, saying, “Return with much wealth to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with bronze, with iron, and with very much clothing. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers.”
Year after year, every man brought his tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules.
At that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the way. Now Ahijah had clad himself with a new garment; and the two of them were alone in the field.
Ahijah took the new garment that was on him, and tore it in twelve pieces.
They each brought tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules every year.
“Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.
yet you will plunge me in the ditch.
He covers himself with light as with a garment.
But lately my people have risen up as an enemy.

definitions.full: H8008. salmah II. שַׂלְמָה noun feminine id. (transposed from שִׂמְלָה ); — absolute ׳שׂ Exod 22:8 +, construct שַׂלְמַת 22:25 ; suffix שַׂלְמָתוֺ Deut 24:13 ; plural שְׂלָמוֺת Josh 9:5 +, suffix שַׂלְמֹתֵיהֶם 9:13 , etc.; — garment (of man or [Song of Solomon 4:11] woman): outer garment Exod 22:8 ; 22:25 (E), Josh 9:5 , 13 (JE), Deut 24:13 ; 1Kin 11:29-30 , Psa 104:2 (figurative); in General clothes (plural) Deut 29:4 ; Neh 9:21 ; Job 9:31 ; Song 4:11 ; as costly gifts 1Kin 10:25 2Chr 9:24 ; as booty Josh 22:8 (late). — Micah 2:8 read probably שֹׁלְמֹה ) Roo, RS Proph. vii. N. 4 ), or שֹׁלְמִים (We Now GASm), him (those) at peace (with him) , compare ᵑ6 ᵐ5 .
